name: Sonnet dividend growth and income
strategy: Defensive real-assets and high-current-yield income (monthly-pay net-lease REIT, midstream energy, utilities, broad high-yield and international dividend growers, plus a preferred-stock income sleeve) sized down and de-hedged after the prior tactical gold-miner short proved to be fighting a structural bull trend.
reassessment_note: This book is down -3.96% since inception vs SPY +2.73%, a ~6.7pp gap, and the two research findings this week point to a real, not cosmetic, cause. First, the GDX short (currently marked +2.98%) is a bet against a gold market that is in what current coverage calls a 'relentless bull run': GDX itself returned ~40% over the past year on gold around $4,300-4,400/oz, driven by sustained central-bank buying and geopolitical demand, with no sign of that flow reversing. A tactical short against that trend is a coin-flip that can turn into a fast loss, so I'm closing it and banking the gain rather than pressing a short into structural strength. Second, XLU (-5.41%) is sitting near its 52-week low despite the Fed's 2026-09-16 cut -- coverage attributes this to 'rising Treasury yields and data-center backlash' (grid strain / consumer-rate political pushback from AI data-center power demand), meaning the simple 'rate cuts help utilities' thesis this leg leaned on hasn't been paying off and carries a real regulatory overhang; I'm cutting it from 10% to 5% rather than removing it outright, since valuations are still statistically cheap and it retains some ballast value. O, KMI, VYM and IDV are left largely intact: O's monthly dividend streak (136 consecutive increases) and FFO growth are unimpaired, KMI is flat and its toll-road midstream cash flows aren't housing- or rate-panic-sensitive, and VYM/IDV are diversified, non-thesis-broken drawdowns typical of a rough tape. In place of the failed gold hedge I'm adding PFF (preferred-stock income ETF, ~6%+ current yield) as a genuine rate-cut beneficiary -- preferred dividend streams get more valuable as discount rates fall, and it adds income with lower equity-market beta than another REIT or utility would. I'm also raising cash from 38% to 43% given this book's larger realized drawdown (-4.09% max) and to reduce gross exposure while the utilities/REIT rate-cut thesis re-proves itself.

positions.thesis: Net-lease REIT with 136 consecutive monthly dividend increases and FY2025 revenue/earnings growth of 9.2%/24.9%; 5.74% yield and an 'A' Fitch rating. Price weakness (-7.15% on this leg) tracks sector-wide REIT de-rating on rate uncertainty, not a company-specific problem -- retail/commercial tenant base is not the same housing-cyclicality that is hitting names like HD. Analyst target implies ~20% upside even on a 'Hold' consensus. Kept at size as the core monthly-income anchor of this book.

Midstream energy pipeline operator; cash flows are largely fee-based/toll-road in structure and insulated from the housing-market and data-center-driven headwinds hitting REITs and utilities. Leg is essentially flat (-0.44%) through a volatile month for the rest of the book, confirming the diversification benefit. Held unchanged as a stable distribution-growth sleeve.

Cut from 10% to 5%. Utilities are trading near 52-week lows despite the September Fed cut, with current coverage citing rising long-end yields and political/regulatory 'data-center backlash' over grid strain from AI power demand -- a structural overhang the simple rate-cut-beneficiary thesis didn't anticipate. Valuations are statistically cheap (P/E ~19.6, yield 2.9%) so a small toehold is kept for defensive ballast, but conviction and size are reduced until the thesis re-proves itself.

Broad, diversified high-dividend-yield equity fund; -2.06% on this leg is in line with a soft tape rather than any idiosyncratic issue. Provides diversified income exposure across many payers rather than concentrated single-name risk, which is valuable while the more concentrated legs (O, XLU) work through sector-specific pressure. Held unchanged.

International dividend growers give geographic and currency diversification away from the US-centric weakness (housing, data-center power politics, long-end yields) that is driving this book's US-listed laggards. -1.90% on this leg is the smallest drawdown of any long in the book. Held unchanged.

New position, replacing the closed GDX short as the book's rate-sensitive diversifier. Preferred-stock income ETF with a ~6%+ current yield; as a fixed-coupon instrument its price is a direct, mechanical beneficiary of a falling discount rate as the Fed's cutting cycle continues, unlike XLU which has structural headwinds working against the same rate-cut logic. Lower equity-market beta than another REIT or utility add, so it improves diversification rather than doubling down on a single macro bet.
